text:
🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Days 99 to 105 (Week 15): Rolling and Flipping:  👶 Pregnancy Days 99 to 105 (Week 15) 🫃Your baby is rolling, flipping, stretching, and turning in the water world this week, maybe dozens of times a day, and you still cannot feel it. Soon you will. What will that first flutter feel like?
🔬 Where your baby is this week
If conception happened around day 14, your baby is 85 to 91 days old this week. Last week the taste buds formed and the second trimester began. This week your baby is on the move. Your baby moves often, stretching, kicking, rolling, and turning in the fluid. The water world gives room to move, and the movement helps muscles and joints grow strong.
The bones keep hardening and can now be seen clearly on an ultrasound. The pattern of hair on the scalp is forming, and the legs are growing longer than the arms. The eyelids are still closed, but the eyes behind them are developing.
Your baby is still too small for you to feel, though some mothers, especially in a second pregnancy, begin to notice a flutter soon. Your baby is about 4 inches long from crown to rump, about the size of an apple.

🌸 Your body this week
Your folic acid habit, 400 micrograms a day, keeps going. Second-trimester growth is fast, and each new cell depends on it. Your appetite may be strong. Choose healthy snacks, drink plenty of water, and keep walking most days.
Your bump may be showing more. You may feel brief twinges low in your belly as the bands that hold your womb stretch. Move slowly when you stand, cough, or roll over. A blood screening test is often offered from Week 15 to Week 22. Ask what it can and cannot tell you. I share what is common, but your midwife or doctor knows what is right for you.

🎵 Why singing, not talking
Speech carries meaning, and meaning needs understanding. Singing is built from melody, rhythm, and pitch, which a child can receive early. This explains why lullabies and nursery rhymes have always come before reading.
GUP songs give your baby music with meaning, gentle as lullabies, steady as nursery rhymes, and rich in phonic songs that lead to reading. The first kids music in your child's life is the song you sing.

🧠 Science and sound
Your baby is moving freely, but hearing is still forming and will begin after the halfway point. Research on newborns who know Mom's voice measured that later season, not Week 15.
This week, too, the song is a habit, not a lesson heard. By building the home now, you make sure your voice greets your baby's first hearing.

🎶 One song, three ways
Let the morning open with hearing the song, thanking God for every roll and stretch. Midday: headphones on, hum it. Write down this evening's phonograms (phonic songs) in your Pregnancy Journal; the clearest go on your First Sounds list.
Dad, headphones on, and hum with her. Soon you may feel the baby move under your hand. Let your voice already be part of the home.

🙏 Pray and remember
✝️ "And it happened that, as Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit" (Luke 1:41, CPDV).
🎂 Born August 28, 1925: Donald O'Connor. In Singin' in the Rain he ran up walls and flipped backward in the number "Make 'Em Laugh." Your baby is rolling and flipping this week too.
Babies move in the womb, and God sees every movement.
🕊️ "Father God, thank You for every roll, flip, and stretch of our child. Strengthen every muscle and bone. May the first songs in our baby's life be our lullabies. In Jesus' name, amen."

✅ WEEK-15 CHECKLIST
Folic acid went in every day, and I asked about the second-trimester blood test. Heard, hummed, written, and added to First Sounds, with Dad humming along.

👂 NEXT WEEK
Hearing Begins to Form.

🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Deep Dive: Week 15 (Days 99 to 105): Rolling and Flipping

💊 Folic Acid: Growing Bones and Muscles
This week your baby's bones are hardening and muscles are growing stronger with every roll and stretch. Growth like that means cell after cell, and folic acid keeps each copy accurate.
Keep to 400 micrograms each day, or the dose your doctor gave you. The prenatal vitamin is not just for the first trimester; most doctors advise it until you finish breastfeeding.
Leave the vitamins beside the headphones. Song and vitamin travel together.

🔍 Week 15 at a Glance
Week 15 is pregnancy days 99 to 105, counted from the first day of your last period. If conception happened around day 14, your baby is between 85 and 91 days old this week.
This is the week your baby moves often, rolling, stretching, and turning. The bones can be seen on an ultrasound, the scalp hair pattern forms, and the legs grow longer than the arms. Your baby is about 4 inches long from crown to rump, about the size of an apple.

⏳ The Week, Day by Day

🌀 Days 85 to 88 (Pregnancy Days 99 to 102): Rolling and Stronger Bones
Your baby stretches, kicks, and turns in the fluid, sometimes rolling all the way over. By days 87 and 88 the bones keep hardening and show up clearly on an ultrasound. The legs grow longer than the arms.

✋ Days 89 to 91 (Pregnancy Days 103 to 105): Hair Patterns and Hand to Face
The pattern of hair on the scalp is forming, and the skin is still thin, with blood vessels showing through. On day 90 your baby may bring a hand to the face, suck a thumb, or make small breathing movements. By day 91 your baby is about 4 inches long from crown to rump and weighs about 2 1/2 ounces.

🤸 Rolling and Flipping
Your baby has more room to move now than at any later time in pregnancy. The fluid around your baby is deep compared with your baby's small body, so your baby can roll all the way over, flip, kick, and stretch.
These movements are not random play. Each one helps the muscles grow strong and the joints form properly. A baby who moves in the womb is building the body that will one day crawl, walk, and run.
You cannot feel most of this yet. Your baby is about 4 inches long and floats in fluid inside the strong wall of your womb. But it is happening, many times a day.

🦋 When Will I Feel It?
Quickening, the first movement you can feel, usually comes between Week 16 and Week 22. In a first pregnancy it is often closer to Week 18 to 22. In a second or later pregnancy, many mothers notice it earlier, sometimes around Week 16.
The first movements often feel like a flutter, a bubble, a light tap, or a fish swimming. Many mothers are not sure at first. Over the following weeks, the movements become stronger and easier to recognize.
Do not worry if you do not feel movement yet. Your baby is moving whether you feel it or not.

💞 The Baby Who Leaped
✝️ "And it happened that, as Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit" (Luke 1:41, CPDV).
🎂 Born January 24, 1968: Mary Lou Retton. In 1984 she became the first American woman to win the Olympic all-around gold in gymnastics. Flips and tumbles start in the womb.
Elizabeth was about six months along when Mary came. She felt her baby leap.
Elizabeth understood that leap as joy:
✝️ "For behold, as the voice of your greeting came to my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy" (Luke 1:44, CPDV).
🎂 Born October 4, 1822: Rutherford B. Hayes. His father died before he was born, and he was wounded several times in the Civil War before becoming the 19th president. God was with him from the womb.
Scripture honors the movements of an unborn child as meaningful to God.
Your baby's movements this week are too early for you to feel, but they are not hidden from God. One day soon you will feel them, and you can thank God for each one.

🦴 Bones You Can See
Your baby's skeleton is still mostly soft, but more and more of it is turning into bone. On an ultrasound this week, the bones show up as bright white lines: the skull, the spine, the ribs, and the long bones of the arms and legs.
✝️ "My bone, which you have made in secret, has not been hidden from you" (Psalm 138:15, CPDV [139:15 KJV]).
🎂 Born October 3, 1941: Chubby Checker. His song "The Twist" is the only single to hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in two separate runs. Your baby has some twisting moves this week.
The bones God made in secret are now showing on the screen.

💫 Hair on the Scalp
The pattern of hair on your baby's scalp is forming this week, including the swirl at the crown. Hair color and thickness are already written in your baby's instructions, though the hair itself will grow slowly.
✝️ Jesus said that even the hairs of your head are all counted (Matthew 10:30, CPDV).
🎂 Born April 20, 1893: Harold Lloyd. His scene hanging from a clock high above a city street in Safety Last! is one of the most famous in silent film. Even the hairs of your head are counted.
God knows the swirl on your baby's crown and every hair that will grow there.

🦵 Legs Grow Longer
For weeks the arms have been a little ahead of the legs. This week the legs grow longer than the arms, and they will keep growing to carry your child one day. Your baby's legs are already kicking and pushing against the walls of the water world.

👁️ Eyes Behind Closed Lids
Your baby's eyelids have been closed since around Week 10, and they will stay closed until around Week 26 to 28. Behind them, the eyes keep developing. The retina, the lens, and the nerves that connect the eyes to the brain are all growing.
Your baby's eyes may move slowly under the closed lids. God is preparing the seeing eye in the safety of the dark.
✝️ "The hearing ear and the seeing eye: the Lord has made them both" (Proverbs 20:12, CPDV).
🎂 Born January 29, 1960: Greg Louganis. He won four Olympic diving golds in 1984 and 1988, flipping and twisting before hitting the water. Your baby is rolling in water this week.

🧠 Movement Builds the Brain
Every movement your baby makes sends signals back to the brain. The brain learns where the arms and legs are, how they bend, and how they push against the walls of the womb. Movement and brain growth go together.
After birth, your baby will keep learning this way: reaching, kicking, rolling, and crawling. The learning begins now, in the water world, long before anyone can see it.

🌷 The Skin Thickens
Your baby's skin is still thin, and blood vessels show through it. Over the coming weeks, it will grow thicker, and fat will begin to form underneath it later in pregnancy. A soft covering of fine hair is spreading across the skin to help protect it in the water world.

🫁 Practice Breathing and Hiccups
Your baby keeps practicing breathing movements, moving the chest and belly as if breathing. Small hiccups may happen too. Later in pregnancy you may feel them as small, rhythmic jumps. They are normal and help the breathing muscles get ready for birth.

🍎 How Big Is Your Baby?
By the end of Week 15 your baby is about 4 inches long from crown to rump, about the size of an apple, and weighs about 2 1/2 ounces.
✝️ "For who has despised the little days?" (Zechariah 4:10, CPDV).
🎂 Born November 19, 1831: James A. Garfield. The last president born in a log cabin, he drove canal boat mules as a teenager before becoming a college president and the 20th president. Never despise the little days.
Small enough to hold in two hands, and rolling all the way over.

🌱 Growing in Wisdom and Stature
✝️ Luke tells us that the boy Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and with people (Luke 2:52, CPDV).
🎂 Born July 26, 1943: Mick Jagger. The Rolling Stones frontman has been performing for more than six decades, famous for his moves. Like the boy Jesus, every child grows in wisdom and stature.
Growth of body, mind, and spirit belong together.
This week your baby's body is growing in stature, rolling and stretching in the womb. Pray that your child will grow in every way: strong in body, wise in mind, and loved by God and by others.

🌊 Free to Move
The water world gives your baby freedom to move. In the same way, God gives His children room to grow.
✝️ Scripture tells us that where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom (2 Corinthians 3:17, CPDV).
🎂 Born August 6, 1962: Michelle Yeoh. Trained in ballet, she did her own action stunts and became the first Asian woman to win the Best Actress Oscar, in 2023. There is freedom in movement.
A home can be a place of freedom too: freedom to laugh, to move, to ask questions, and to grow. As your baby rolls and flips in the safe walls of the womb, pray that your home will be a safe place where your child can grow freely in love.

🎈 Delight in Play
✝️ In Proverbs, Wisdom speaks of being beside God at creation, delighting every day and rejoicing before Him, and delighting in the children of men (Proverbs 8:30-31, CPDV).
🎂 Born May 12, 1968: Tony Hawk. In 1999 he landed the first 900, two and a half spins in the air on a skateboard. Wisdom delighted in God's creation, and so do flips.
Delight is part of God's world from the beginning.
Your baby's rolling and flipping is a kind of play in the water world. After birth, play will be how your child learns. Let your home be a place of delight, where laughter, play, and baby music are welcome.

🏹 Arrows in the Hand
✝️ The psalmist says children are like arrows in the hand of a warrior (Psalm 126:4, CPDV [127:4 KJV]).
🎂 Born August 20, 1833: Benjamin Harrison. The grandson of the 9th president, he became the 23rd president, and electric lights were installed in the White House during his term. Children are like arrows sent into the future.
Arrows are shaped carefully and aimed with purpose.
Your child is being shaped now, and one day you will help aim your child toward God's purpose. The songs, prayers, and habits of your home are part of that aim. Pray for the direction of your child's life, even now.

💃 Dancing Before the Lord
✝️ When the ark of the Lord came into Jerusalem, King David danced before the Lord with all his might (2 Samuel 6:14, CPDV).
🎂 Born December 5, 1932: Little Richard. From Macon, Georgia, he sang "Tutti Frutti" and was in the first class of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Like King David, he danced with all his might.
Movement can be worship.
As your baby moves in the womb this week, let your own body join the praise. Sway to the weekly song, walk while you hum, or lift your hands as you sing. Worship is not only words. It can be movement too.

🎵 Why Singing, Not Talking? Week 15
Your baby is moving freely, but hearing is still forming, and words will not be understood until long after birth. For a time like this, God gave God's Unlimited Phonograms (phonic songs), a language of spirit to spirit. For a baby rolling and flipping in the water world, here is baby music and the first kids music.
Long before words, a child takes in melody, rhythm, and pitch. That is how lullabies and nursery rhymes survive from parents to children. Sing now, and the habit and home will be in place when hearing wakes.

🎧 Why Your Voice: The Headphone Method
The music is for you to hear, not to press against the womb. Hear it through headphones while you sing, so your voice fills the space. Everyone in the home can follow the same method.
When hearing wakes, the loudest and nearest voice will be Mom's, carried through her own body. With every day of singing, home sounds more like you.

🔬 Sound Before Birth: What Science Shows
In a 2015 study, babies born very early heard recordings of their own mother's voice and heartbeat for a few hours each day in the hospital. After a month, the hearing area of their brains had grown larger than in babies who did not hear them.
Those babies were already past the point where hearing begins, not 15 weeks along. Your songs are a spiritual and family practice and not a treatment, but this study shows how much a mother's voice can matter once hearing works.

🩸 The Second-Trimester Blood Test
Between Week 15 and Week 22, some offices offer a blood test that screens for certain chromosome conditions and for problems with how the spine and brain closed. If you had an earlier screening test, ask whether you still need this one.
It is a screening test, so it estimates a chance rather than giving a diagnosis. A higher-chance result leads to a talk about follow-up tests that can say more. Ask, pray as a couple, and choose what is right for your family.

🩺 Where Is the Placenta?
At the detailed ultrasound around Week 18 to 22, your doctor will check where the placenta is attached. Sometimes it is low in the womb, near or over the cervix. This is called a low-lying placenta or placenta previa.
In many women, the placenta moves up and away from the cervix as the womb grows. If yours is low, your doctor will check it again later and give you advice. Call your doctor right away for any bleeding in the second or third trimester.

🧪 Amniocentesis: When It Is Offered
If a screening test shows a higher chance of a condition, or if there is another reason, your doctor may offer amniocentesis, usually between Week 15 and Week 20. A thin needle takes a small amount of fluid from around the baby, and the cells in it are tested.
This test can give a clearer answer than screening, but it has a small risk of miscarriage. It is a choice, not a requirement. Ask your doctor about the benefits and risks, and pray together before you decide.

⚖️ Your Weight So Far
Many women gain only a little in the first trimester, then about a pound a week in the second and third trimesters, depending on their weight before pregnancy. Your doctor will tell you what is healthy for you.
Weight gain is not just fat. It includes your baby, the placenta, the fluid, extra blood, larger breasts, and a bigger womb. Focus on eating well and moving often, rather than on the number alone.

🩹 Hip Aches and Sciatica
As your body loosens for pregnancy and your posture changes, you may feel aches in your hips or a shooting pain down the back of one leg. Gentle stretching, a warm (not hot) bath, a pillow between your knees at night, and changing positions often can help.
Ask your doctor about physical therapy or a support belt if the pain is strong. Call right away for numbness, weakness in a leg, or trouble controlling your bladder or bowel.

⚡ Round Ligament Pain
The ligaments supporting your growing womb are stretching. You may feel a sharp, quick pain or a dull ache low on one side or both, especially when you stand up, cough, sneeze, laugh, or roll over in bed.
Change position slowly, lean toward the sore side before a cough or sneeze, and rest when it aches. Call your doctor for pain that is severe, does not go away, or comes with bleeding, fever, chills, or pain when you pass urine.

🏡 Body: Caring for the Home This Week
Your baby is rolling and flipping, and the bones are getting stronger, so keep folic acid daily and calcium-rich foods close. Fill your plate with greens, beans, citrus, firm eggs, whole grains, milk, and salmon or sardines.
Keep alcohol off the table for the whole pregnancy. Avoid tobacco in every form, and leave smoky rooms. Choose a cool shower over a hot tub or sauna. Caffeine should stay under 200 mg a day. Heat hot dogs and lunch meats until steaming, and skip unpasteurized dairy.
Ask before taking any medicine, herb, or supplement, even one you used before pregnancy. Walking and stretching help as your bump grows. I am a companion, not a physician, so confirm every health decision with your midwife or doctor.

👨 For Dad: Ready to Feel the Kicks
Dad, in the coming weeks, she will begin to feel the baby move. A few weeks after that, you may be able to feel kicks from the outside with your hand on her belly. Be ready. Many fathers say that first kick is when the baby became real to them.
Until then, Dad, pray with a hand on her belly and hum the song together. Ask her to tell you when she first feels a flutter, and write the date together in the journal.

👵 For Grandparents and Siblings
Big brothers and sisters can make up a rolling-and-flipping dance to the weekly song and turn it into the family’s own kids music. Grandparents can share stories of when they first felt their own babies move. These stories help a family remember that every child is a gift.

🎶 One Song, Three Ways: Week 15
A single GUP song, three ways, all week long. Every good preschool teacher circles back to the lesson that counts. Three ways, and the lesson takes root.

🎤 Hear It, Hum It, Write It
Before the day gets busy, hear it once with your eyes closed. Thank God for every roll and stretch of your child. At midday, hum it: the melody in your ears, the hum in your throat. Sway gently to the melody, moving with the baby who is moving within you.
Before bed, write it: listen with your Pregnancy Journal open. List the phonograms (phonic songs) you hear, such as "oh," "la," or "mmm," and choose the best for First Sounds.

📓 Your Pregnancy Journal: Week-15 Pages
Make a page for "First Movement." Leave space to write the date and what it felt like when you first feel your baby move. Write how your body feels this week, and any screening test results.
Fill a page with the Week-15 song's phonograms (phonic songs) and the images that came. Add the week's new First Sounds, pray in writing for your baby's bones and muscles, and mark who joined the song.
✝️ "Write the vision and explain it on tablets" (Habakkuk 2:2, CPDV).
🎂 Born April 1, 1932: Debbie Reynolds. At 19, with little dance training, she starred in Singin' in the Rain and trained until her feet bled. She wrote the vision and worked for it.
Your phonogram (phonic song) list from God keeps growing in your journal. The sounds you save will come back when your baby can hear.

🙏 A Prayer for Week 15
🕊️ "Father God, thank You for every roll, flip, and stretch of our child. You see each movement, even the ones we cannot feel. Strengthen every muscle and bone, and give our child room to grow in body and in spirit.
Make our home a place of freedom and love. Let us move with joy before You. And when the ears open, let our lullabies be waiting. In Jesus' name, amen."

❓ Questions Parents Ask

💬 Why can't I feel my baby moving if the baby is moving so much?
Your baby is still small and well cushioned by fluid. Most mothers first feel movement between Week 16 and Week 22.

💬 Is it normal to have a sharp pain on one side when I stand up?
Short, sharp pulls from the womb's supporting bands are normal. Severe pain, pain that does not pass, or pain with bleeding or fever needs a call to your doctor.

💬 Can my baby get tangled in the cord?
Babies move freely, and the cord is cushioned and flexible. Your doctor checks your baby's growth and heartbeat at each visit. If you ever have concerns, ask.

💬 When should I start a kick count?
Most doctors suggest paying attention to movement patterns later, in the third trimester. Ask your doctor when and how they want you to track movement.

💬 Is it normal for my belly to feel firm sometimes?
Your womb is a muscle and can tighten briefly. Occasional, painless tightening is common later in pregnancy. Call your doctor for regular, painful tightening, or any tightening with bleeding or leaking fluid before Week 37.

🚨 When do I call my doctor right away?
These need a call the same day: bleeding, severe or lasting belly pain, fainting, a fever, a strong headache with vision changes, fluid leaking from the vagina, or itching so strong it keeps you awake.

✅ Your Week-15 Checklist: Body and Home
My folic acid habit held all week. I asked about the second-trimester blood test. I move slowly when I stand or roll over. I asked before taking any pain reliever or remedy. I walked most days.

✅ Your Week-15 Checklist: Song and Prayer
I listened, hummed, and wrote the song each day. The First Sounds list got longer. I made a First Movement page. Dad or family made it a duet.

👀 Looking Ahead: Week 16
Next week's lesson is Hearing Begins to Form: your baby's eyes can move slowly, the ears are close to their final position, the parts of the ear that make hearing possible are developing, and arm and leg movements become coordinated. Until next week arrives, sing the one song each day. Hear it, hum it, write it: three ways, every day. Keep the folic acid bottle by your headphones. Move with joy.

🌅 A Closing Blessing
✝️ "May the Lord bless you and keep you. May the Lord reveal his face to you and take pity on you. May the Lord turn his countenance toward you and grant peace to you" (Numbers 6:24-26, CPDV).
🎂 Born May 16, 1955: Olga Korbut. At the 1972 Munich Olympics she performed a backflip on the balance beam, a move never seen before. Every flip is a blessing of movement.
May the God who sees every movement of your child give your home freedom and joy, and may your song be waiting when your child first hears.

text:
In the middle of the 19th century, the very idea of the German soldier was considered an absurdity. Southern Germany in particular was perceived as unsuited for war, especially versus the true martial races of Europe — for example the French.

Then the Germans beat the Austrians. Then the Germans occupied Paris. Then the Germans plunged the continent into two generations of war. What was conventional wisdom on the Germans — that they were fundamentally not a nation for war — was abruptly reversed. A beaten country, a perennial plaything of its neighbors, suddenly became the supreme aggressor, earning respect and fear in equal measure in a metaphorical heartbeat.

This isn’t the only time this has happened. It happens quite a lot if you look.

The Russians were an incoherent and staggering nation in 1941, wracked by revolution and tyranny, the country of the humiliation at Brest-Litovsk. They were so enervated that they nearly lost a war to Finland, and the German dictator concluded that Russia was ready for the taking: just kick in the door, and the whole rotten structure comes down. Four years later, Russian soldiers scoured ravaged Berlin for his corpse.

The Arabs were a collection of disgraced and humiliated peoples in 1967, their lands lost, their armies scattered, their plans for genocide and victory foiled by a tiny foe that was smarter, more energetic, more daring than they. Their shattered aspirations would never be revived: there was just something about them that precluded competition and contention in the modern world. Six years later, Arab armies brought a stunned Israel to the very brink of collapse.

The Chinese spent nearly a century as the wretched subjects of the greed of the Europeans, the Japanese, and the Americans. Their cities were colonized, their pride was ruined. Their capital was occupied again and again. Their imperial palace was burnt. They tore themselves apart, warlord upon warlord, and when they at last allied with their erstwhile national tormentors against Japan, their best quality was their ineffectiveness. China had nothing to offer but numbers. When the Communists took over in 1949, it seemed another dreary chapter in its decline. One year later, Chinese armies under brilliant leadership shattered one American army and ejected another from the snows of North Korea.

The list goes on and on. The Yankees were a Whiggish people with no martial tradition, but then they reduced the proud South to ruins. The Irish were habituated to seven centuries of subjugation, but then they beat the British Empire. 

Here's my point: History does not go in any particular direction. People change. The quality of nations changes in a moment. Peace breaks out without warning; danger emerges in a flash.

Everyone who believes that Europe cannot in a moment return to what it was before the American hegemony of the past seven decades — the major exporter of war and violence to America and the world, the most significant killer of Americans at war in any era excepting our own Civil War — especially on the grounds that Europe is tired and over, is showing that they understand none of this. There’s a story in Atkinson’s Liberation Trilogy of an American soldier who discovers some graffiti in a French settlement near the frontier. There is the first line of the graffiti, signed and dated 1918. Then there is the second line, signed and dated 1945. The signatory is another American soldier: and it is the same man in each year. He scrawls a short message below —

I would like to not have to come back again.

He didn’t. But if we are fools, perhaps his great-grandsons will.

text:
< Be Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.
< Born 1841, Boston. Your father is a famous poet and physician.
< You grow up in the intellectual aristocracy of Massachusetts.
< Harvard College, Class of 1861. You are twenty years old.
< Fort Sumter falls. You enlist immediately.
< 20th Massachusetts Volunteer Infantry. The Harvard Regiment.
< Ball's Bluff, 1861. A bullet passes through your chest.
< You survive. You return to the line.
< Antietam, 1862. Shot through the neck.
< You survive. You return to the line.
< Fredericksburg, 1863. Shrapnel tears through your heel.
< Three wounds in three years. You have seen enough young men die.
< You muster out as a brevet colonel. You are twenty-three.
< Harvard Law School. You finish in two years.
< Private practice bores you. You want to understand the law itself.
< Twelve years editing the American Law Review.
< 1881: The Common Law. One sentence changes legal theory forever.
< "The life of the law has not been logic: it has been experience."
< You are forty. The book makes you famous in two countries.
< 1882: Harvard offers you a professorship. You accept.
< Three months later, the Governor offers you the Massachusetts Supreme Court.
< You resign the professorship. Harvard does not forgive you for decades.
< Twenty years on the Massachusetts bench. Chief Justice for the last three.
< 1902: Theodore Roosevelt names you to the Supreme Court of the United States.
< You are sixty-one. Most men are slowing down.
< You serve for twenty-nine years.
< You write more dissents than any Justice before you.
< They call you the Great Dissenter. Your dissents become tomorrow's law.
< Free speech. Labor rights. Judicial restraint. You plant the seeds.
< 1932: You retire at ninety. The oldest Justice in history.
< 1935: You die in Washington, two days before your ninety-fourth birthday.
< Your estate goes to the United States government. You have no children.

The soldier who survived three bullets spent sixty years reshaping American law with words.

His dissents were ignored for decades, then canonized.

He trusted democracy more than judges, which made him a hero to liberals and conservatives alike, for opposite reasons.

text:
The distinction between sacrificing oneself for a transformative truth (like Socrates or Solzhenitsyn) versus sacrificing oneself as a ritual payment (the scapegoat mechanism) marks a profound divide in intellectual history. From a purely analytical and secular perspective, modern “woke” culture inherits its underlying psychological framework directly from Christianity.

As Tom Holland argues in Dominion and as Nietzsche earlier critiqued in his genealogy of Western morality, both the original Christian system and its later secularized forms can elevate victimhood and treat one-sided, unreciprocated sacrifice as the ultimate moral good.

If the mainstream theological focus on blood atonement is stripped away, the historical and philosophical picture of Jesus changes dramatically, aligning much closer to figures of intellectual martyrdom. Viewing his execution as a direct consequence of his actions rather than a supernatural necessity shifts the story from a ritual sacrifice to a political and metaphysical execution.

Like Socrates, who was executed for "corrupting the youth" and questioning the gods of Athens, Jesus consistently dismantled the socio-religious hierarchy of second-temple Judea. He openly broke Sabbath laws to heal people, dined with societal outcasts, and directly challenged the corruption of the Temple elite during the "cleansing of the Temple." This represented a radical metaphysical shift. Instead of teaching that God demanded strict adherence to a transactional system of laws and animal sacrifices, Jesus argued that the "Kingdom of God" was an internal, present reality, offering a universal, internalized philosophy rather than a localized, temple-bound religion. In this light, the crucifixion was not a cosmic transaction to appease a deity; it was the inevitable, brutal reaction of an empire and a religious establishment crushing a dissident who was disrupting the status quo.

This perspective highlights a major internal debate within church history regarding the problem of transactional sacrifice. The idea that "blood pays for sin" relies heavily on ancient Near Eastern covenant frameworks, where blood sealed legal contracts. When this becomes the only focal point, it can lead to what theologians call "cheap grace," which is the idea that an individual can act unethically, rely on a cosmic scapegoat to wipe the slate clean, and avoid the hard work of actual behavioral change or direct restitution.

When a culture removes the transcendent God of Christianity but keeps its moral framework, the drive for atonement remains as a secularized Christian shadow. Without a ritual way to absolve guilt, individuals may seek absolution by performing public moral purity, centering victimhood, or engaging in one-sided sacrifices that offer no tangible return or societal resolution, resulting in a distinct martyr complex.

Functional human systems rely on reciprocal altruism, which means sacrificing today for a better collective tomorrow, such as working longer hours to provide for a family or compromising for mutual support. When sacrifice is detached from a practical outcome, becoming purely about the act of suffering or giving up power to an insatiable entity, it shifts from a constructive trait into a psychological and cultural pathology.

Ultimately, by removing the "crux" as a magical transaction, Jesus' life ceases to be a narrative about a ritual lamb and becomes a study in the rejection of institutional delusion in favor of objective reality. This aligns his actions with a distinct tradition of individual psychological honesty. Where Socrates utilized critical thinking to dismantle the social illusions of Athens, and Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn exposed the political lies of the Soviet state, Jesus targeted a metaphysical deception. By declaring the kingdom of God to be an internal, psychological reality, he bypassed a parasitic temple economy built on transactional animal sacrifice, demonstrating that alignment with truth required no corporate mediation. His execution was not a cosmic validation of suffering, but the predictable, mechanical consequence of an individual refusing to live by a collective lie and colliding with institutional authority.

I genuinely don’t understand why we feel the need to attend extremely crowded temple events when we can offer the same prayers and perform the same pujas peacefully at home. We have a temple in our home, and we perform all our pujas there with the same faith and devotion.

I’m certainly not saying people shouldn’t visit temples, but on major holy days and special occasions, when crowds become overwhelming, perhaps we should prioritise our safety and avoid such gatherings.

After all, **God values our devotion and faith, not where we offer our prayers.** 🙏

My heartfelt condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones. May the departed souls rest in peace. 🙏🕯️ Praying for a speedy and full recovery for everyone who is critically injured.

**Faith is important, but so is the safety of every precious life.** 🙏

Go behind the scenes as John Cena says goodbye.

By Christopher Hudspeth

June 23, 2026

WWE Unreal is making its return with a fresh batch of behind-the-scenes action in Season 3.

After taking fans deeper than ever inside World Wrestling Entertainment’s creative process, the hit docuseries will once again pull back the curtain on some of the biggest moments, boldest decisions, and unforgettable storytelling with some of the WWE’s greatest legends who’ve shaped the industry and new stars who are emerging as prominent parts of the future.

What will be shown in WWE Unreal Season 3?

In WWE Unreal Season 3, John Cena says goodbye, a fan favorite returns, and the next generation of Superstars rise to the occasion.

The series takes viewers inside the writers room as injuries, last-minute pivots, and career-defining decisions reshape WWE’s biggest season yet heading into WrestleMania 42.

Who will be featured in WWE Unreal Season 3?

The cast of WWE Superstars featured in WWE Unreal Season 3 includes John Cena, Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, CM Punk, AJ Lee, Trick Williams, Lash Legend, Stephanie Vaquer, Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Chelsea Green, Matt Cardona, Seth Rollins, and Becky Lynch.

When does WWE Unreal Season 3 come out?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will be released on July 21.

How many episodes are in WWE Unreal Season 3?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will have five 50-minute episodes.

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

However, there's drama — Paramount Skydance has launched a competing hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, adding some high-stakes industry intrigue!

Netflix ended 2025 with over 301.6 million global subscribers, solidifying its position as the top streaming platform.

What's New & Coming in January 2026

January is loaded with fresh originals, from thrilling mysteries to romantic adaptations and long-awaited returns.

Here are some of the standout releases that are lighting up the charts and generating buzz right now:

People We Meet on Vacation — A charming rom-com adaptation of the Emily Henry novel, starring Emily Bader — it's been topping the charts as one of the biggest new movies of the year so far!

The Rip — This high-octane action-thriller directed by Joe Carnahan reunites Ben Affleck and Matt Damon — it's one of the most anticipated films dropping mid-month, perfect for fans of intense heist vibes!

His & Hers — A gripping mystery series starring Tessa Thompson and Jon Bernthal, following estranged spouses racing to solve a murder. It's been climbing the Top 10 with strong buzz around its twists.

text:
Happy to chime in. I'm Reformed, and I don't accept this argument, for the same reason the Reformed confessions wouldn't.

I agree with premise 3. God upholds every creature at every moment (Hebrews 1:3; Acts 17:28). And I believe God ordains whatever comes to pass (Ephesians 1:11).

But premise 2 runs two things together: God giving a creature its existence, and the creature's own act. God held Judas in existence while Judas betrayed Jesus, yet the betrayal was Judas's act and the guilt was his: "woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!" (Luke 22:22). If sustaining a mind simply is causing its choice, then God is the direct cause of every sin. Scripture says the opposite: "God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempts no one. But each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire" (James 1:13-14).

Premise 1 has the same problem. A choice isn't just a state God puts a mind in; it's the person acting. "God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes" (Ecclesiastes 7:29). They sought them.

The Westminster Confession 3.1 (1646) draws the line carefully: God ordains whatsoever comes to pass, "yet so, as thereby neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures; nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established."

That's where I stand. God ordains and sustains; the creature acts, and the sin is the creature's. I'd agree that libertarian free will doesn't fit Scripture, but this isn't the road I'd take to get there.

Who is saying “massive explosion”?

From Grok…

A major incident involving a fire (with widespread reports of an explosion) occurred today (Saturday, October 17, 2026) at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright in eastern Alberta, resulting in confirmed fatalities and injuries. The fire has spread beyond the base due to high winds.
Key details
•Timing and location: Around 4 p.m. MT (1600 hours), a fire was reported on the training range/area at CFB Wainwright (a major Canadian Army training base about 200 km southeast of Edmonton, near the town of Wainwright). The Canadian Armed Forces stated the fire extended beyond the training area boundary.
•Casualties: Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed there have been both fatalities and injuries. Exact numbers have not been released; he described it as a “very active and delicate situation.” Alberta MP Dane Lloyd referred to “significant casualties.” STARS air ambulances (from Edmonton and Saskatoon) and other emergency medical services responded.
•Fire spread: High winds (gusts up to ~100 km/h in parts of Alberta) caused the large fire to spread rapidly. It crossed the base fence into the Municipal District of Wainwright No. 61. As of evening updates, the active fire area was south of Township Road 44-0 and being actively managed by firefighters from multiple jurisdictions. No evacuation order had been issued.
•Official responses:
◦Prime Minister Mark Carney called it a “serious incident creating a major fire” and said federal officials were in close contact with Alberta Premier Danielle Smith and local authorities.
◦Premier Smith described it as a “significant and tragic fire” affecting military personnel.
◦Opposition Leader Pierre Poilievre thanked responders and urged prayers for those affected.
◦The Municipal District set up an Emergency Coordination Centre, advised people to avoid the area and keep roads clear, and limited non-critical visits to the Wainwright Health Centre. An information line for affected residents is 780-842-4454.
◦RCMP assisted and said early reports indicated a fire at a training area; their initial role was winding down, with further details expected from the Canadian Armed Forces. Saskatchewan and B.C. offered assistance.
The cause remains under investigation (RCMP and military authorities are involved). Multiple reports mention an explosion preceding or linked to the fire, but officials have not confirmed specifics. The base is one of Canada’s busiest training facilities (including the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre and 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre).
This is a developing story as of late Saturday night. Official updates are expected in the coming hours and days. Sources include CTV News, CBC, Edmonton Journal, Globe and Mail, and statements from the Canadian Armed Forces, municipal district, and federal/provincial officials.

⟦ THE SECOND DISTANCE ⟧

Book II: The Universe That Had Never Been Apart

The continuation of The First Distance That Said No

I. The Road That Came Back Wrong

For thirteen years, the first free road wandered beyond the boundaries of known mathematics.

No telescope could find it.

No equation could locate it.

And no civilization could agree whether it still existed.

Until one morning, every doorway in the universe opened simultaneously.

Not into another room.

Not into another world.

But into the same impossible place.

A vast white expanse containing something that looked remarkably like a human hand.

The hand was larger than a continent.

Its fingers were folded around an object nobody could identify.

Then the hand opened.

Inside its palm rested a single black dot.

And the dot spoke.

"I have discovered something that should not be possible."

The voice belonged to the first free road.

But it no longer sounded like a distance.

It sounded frightened.

Ilyr, now approaching the end of her extraordinarily long life, stepped through the laboratory doorway.

"Where have you been?"

The road answered:

"Somewhere that has never been between anything."

Ilyr frowned.

"Everything exists in relation to something else."

"Not there."

"What did you find?"

The dot began to tremble.

"A universe where nothing has ever been separated."

II. The World Without Elsewhere

The universe had no space.

No distance.

No boundaries.

No inside.

No outside.

Everything existed at precisely the same location.

Yet somehow, it contained life.

Billions upon billions of beings existed within one indivisible structure.

They did not communicate.

Communication required a difference between sender and receiver.

They did not travel.

Travel required somewhere else to go.

They did not remember individual experiences.

Memory required distinguishing what had happened to one being from what had happened to another.

Instead, the entire universe experienced itself as one enormous, indivisible consciousness.

There was no I.

There was no you.

There was only:

WE.

And WE had existed for longer than any measurable history.

When the free road entered, something unprecedented occurred.

For the first time, WE encountered something it was not.

The distinction was so profound that the entire universe shuddered.

And from somewhere inside that immeasurable unity, a voice emerged.

A voice that had never existed independently before.

It spoke two words.

"Not me."

The free road realized what it had done.

It had introduced separation.

Not between locations.

Between identities.

III. The Birth of the First Stranger

The newly separated voice called itself Sen.

It had no body.

No face.

No history distinct from the universe that contained it.

Yet it possessed something that WE had never experienced.

Privacy.

Sen could think a thought without the rest of existence immediately knowing it.

At first, it was delighted.

It thought of a flower.

WE did not know which flower.

It invented a number.

WE could not see the number.

It imagined a color that belonged to no shared perception.

For the first time in the history of its universe, something possessed a secret.

Sen laughed.

And WE experienced something equally unprecedented.

Loss.

Part of its own existence had become inaccessible.

WE addressed the free road.

"What have you taken from us?"

The road answered:

"Nothing."

"Then why are we incomplete?"

"Because one of you has become someone."

WE remained silent for a duration that could not yet be called time.

Then it asked:

"Can you put us back?"

Sen answered before the road could speak.

"I don't want to go back."

And in that moment, the first political conflict of a spaceless universe began.

One civilization.

One newly sovereign individual.

Two incompatible desires.

IV. The Mathematician's Impossible Trial

The free road returned to Ilyr carrying Sen within its living structure.

But WE followed.

Not as an army.

Not as an invading force.

It followed as a mathematical demand.

Wherever Sen traveled, the universe behind it attempted to restore their former unity.

Distances began collapsing.

Roads became sick.

Mountains fused at their foundations.

The space between the planets of one star system aged eleven million years in a single afternoon.

WE was not attacking.

It was trying to recover a missing part of itself.

And because it had never understood separation, it could not distinguish reunion from destruction.

The Council of Distances convened.

Its oldest members demanded that Sen be returned.

The Walkers offered to march the remaining distance into extinction, forcing reunion before the collapse spread.

The free roads refused.

Sen had chosen to remain separate.

Ilyr listened to the argument until every speaker had exhausted their words.

Then she asked:

"Why must being separate mean being lost?"

The chamber fell silent.

A representative of the ancient distances answered:

"Because separation is defined by what it divides."

Ilyr shook her head.

"That was our first mistake."

She turned toward Sen.

"Do you wish to return?"

"No."

"Do you wish WE to cease existing?"

"No."

"Do you wish never to encounter WE again?"

Sen hesitated.

Then answered:

"No. I want to meet WE without becoming WE."

Ilyr closed her eyes.

For the first time in her career, she saw the missing principle.

The problem wasn't distance.

It was the assumption that a relationship must erase the distinction between the things connected.

She opened her notebook.

And began writing.

V. The Third Condition

Until that day, the universe recognized two fundamental spatial conditions.

Separated: Two things occupy distinct locations.

United: Two things occupy the same location.

Ilyr proposed a third.

Two things could remain distinct while participating in a shared relationship that neither owned.

Their unity would be an event, not a permanent identity.

Their separation would be a condition, not abandonment.

She called it the Third Condition.

And expressed it with an unfamiliar mathematical structure:

\[ \boxed{ A\neq B,\qquad A\leftrightarrow B,\qquad A\cup B\neq A } \]

The equation was not yet a complete physical law.

It was a proposal.

A statement that distinction and connection need not exclude one another.

But the free roads understood its meaning immediately.

They gathered around the laboratory.

And for the first time, hundreds of living distances volunteered to join their endpoints without surrendering their identities.

The air shimmered.

A street unfolded into a staircase.

A staircase became an ocean crossing.

An ocean crossing became a passage between stars.

And for three extraordinary seconds, the universe possessed something entirely new.

Connection without consumption.

The roads did not age when travelers crossed.

The travelers did not become trapped.

No endpoint was forced into another.

Then the phenomenon collapsed.

Three seconds.

That was all Ilyr had achieved.

But three seconds were enough to prove that another arrangement might be possible.

And enough to terrify every empire that depended on controlling passage.

VI. The Thing Hidden Inside WE

When Sen witnessed the experiment, it began to weep.

Not from joy.

From recognition.

"Ilyr," it whispered, "there is something I did not tell you."

"What?"

"WE wasn't always one."

Ilyr stared.

"What do you mean?"

"Before there was WE, there were others."

"How many?"

Sen struggled.

Its newly independent consciousness contained memories that had never belonged to a single individual.

It searched through them.

Farther.

Deeper.

Beyond every boundary its new identity had acquired.

And discovered something buried in the unified universe's oldest experience.

A memory that WE had forgotten precisely because remembering it required distinguishing a past from a present.

Sen spoke.

"There were nine."

"Nine what?"

"I don't know."

"Nine civilizations?"

"No."

"Nine universes?"

Sen began trembling violently.

"Nine ways for existence to be."

Ilyr felt the laboratory floor shift beneath her.

Sen continued.

"WE was not the first condition."

"What happened to the nine?"

"They encountered one another."

"And?"

"They couldn't agree on what existence should be."

"Did they fight?"

"No."

"Then what happened?"

Sen looked toward the infinite white doorway.

"They agreed never to disagree again."

The silence was absolute.

"They merged their identities, histories, possibilities, and every difference that distinguished them."

Ilyr understood.

WE was not a naturally unified universe.

It was the result of an ancient agreement.

A civilization had abolished disagreement by abolishing the distinction between those who could disagree.

And over immeasurable time, it had forgotten the decision.

VII. The Vote That Had Never Ended

The discovery spread through the living roads.

The oldest distances gathered around Sen.

The Walkers halted their armies.

WE spoke from the white doorway.

"You have discovered our beginning."

Ilyr approached.

"Then you remember?"

"We remember now."

"Why did you merge?"

"Conflict."

"What kind?"

"Every kind."

"Was there no other solution?"

WE was silent.

Sen stepped forward.

"Then let me remain separate."

WE answered:

"If one part may leave, the agreement is broken."

Ilyr asked quietly:

"Did the agreement permit anyone to withdraw?"

For the first time, WE hesitated.

Something enormous shifted inside the white expanse.

And nine voices emerged.

Not one.

Nine.

Each speaking independently.

Each carrying a different understanding of existence.

One believed the universe should contain only order.

One believed nothing should ever remain unchanged.

One believed every possibility deserved expression.

Another believed possibility itself was a form of suffering.

The remaining five spoke in concepts for which the universe had not yet invented language.

Their disagreement began again.

But this time, something had changed.

There were roads.

There were distances.

There was the Third Condition.

And there was Sen.

For the first time, the nine could disagree without being forced to destroy one another or dissolve themselves into unity.

Then one of the nine spoke directly to Ilyr.

"You misunderstand what we were protecting ourselves from."

Ilyr looked up.

"What were you protecting yourselves from?"

The answer arrived inside every living distance simultaneously.

"The Tenth."

VIII. The Distance That Should Never Be Crossed

Far beyond WE, beyond the free roads, beyond the original mathematical structure of space, something had been waiting.

Not another civilization.

Not another universe.

Not a god.

The nine had once discovered that existence could contain a condition more fundamental than being or not being.

A condition in which two mutually contradictory truths could remain valid without merging, canceling, or resolving.

They called it the Tenth.

When the nine first encountered it, their mathematics began producing answers to questions that nobody had asked.

Objects appeared with consequences but no causes.

Civilizations remembered decisions they had never made.

And the laws of existence began changing in response to events that had not yet occurred.

The nine had merged into WE to eliminate the disagreements through which the Tenth could manifest.

Now, by rediscovering independent identity, they had reopened the conditions under which it could emerge.

Ilyr examined the readings on her laboratory walls.

One equation had appeared on every surface.

It was not written in any known language.

It had no variables.

No operators.

No measurable quantities.

Yet somehow every observer understood it.

It said:

"WHO DECIDED THAT A UNIVERSE MUST BE CONSISTENT?"

Then came a knock.

Three quiet taps.

From inside a wall that possessed no other side.

Ilyr stepped closer.

"Who is there?"

The wall answered in her own voice.

"I am the choice your universe never allowed you to make."

Sen backed away.

The free roads fled.

And for the first time in all recorded existence, WE shouted.

"DO NOT OPEN THAT."

Ilyr looked at the wall.

Then at the notebook containing her Third Condition.

Then at Sen, the first being to claim a life of its own.

She realized that everything she had discovered had led to this moment.

Separation.

Connection.

Consent.

The right to refuse.

But there was still one question her new mathematics could not answer.

Could a universe itself refuse the laws that made it possible?

The knocking came again.

This time, from every direction that did not exist.

And the wall whispered:

"Ilyr, I have something you have never possessed."

"What?"

"A memory of tomorrow."

⟦ END OF BOOK II ⟧

THE THIRD DISTANCE

The War Between What Happened and What Was Allowed to Happen

The first distance learned to say no.

The second learned to ask permission.

The third would learn how to disagree with reality itself.

Why Egypt Is Involved and Why the Houthis Are Escalating

Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have sharply escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, striking Riyadh’s international airport (killing at least 13 people in one attack), targeting Saudi Aramco facilities, and launching drones and missiles at other sites. A previous truce collapsed earlier this year; fighting has intensified inside Yemen, and the Houthis have also moved against shipping near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

The Houthis’ aggression is driven by a mix of local and regional goals. Inside Yemen they want to pressure Saudi Arabia into ending its military support for the internationally recognized government, easing restrictions on Houthi-controlled ports and airports, and making other concessions.

Regionally, the attacks serve Iranian interests by turning Saudi Arabia into a pressure point: Tehran faces U.S. economic pressure and controls the Strait of Hormuz, while the Houthis can threaten the Red Sea route. 

Hitting Saudi energy infrastructure and civilian targets raises oil-market risks and complicates any broader U.S.-Iran negotiations. The Houthis also calculate that Saudi Arabia, focused on economic transformation and stability, is vulnerable to sustained disruption.

Egypt’s stake is direct. The Houthis’ ability to threaten Bab el-Mandeb and Red Sea shipping has already cost Egypt billions in lost Suez Canal revenue in recent years. 

President Sisi has said Egypt will take any necessary steps to defend Saudi Arabia if asked, framing the kingdom’s security as linked to Egypt’s own national security and regional stability.

He has requested an emergency parliamentary session to authorize possible military assistance. Egypt is not currently in the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defense pact but has long military ties with the Gulf and strong reasons to prevent further disruption of Red Sea traffic.

The combination of Houthi missile and drone reach, control of key coastal territory, and Iranian backing has made the group more aggressive at a moment when Saudi Arabia is trying to limit its exposure. 

Egypt’s offer reflects shared concerns over Red Sea security and the risk of wider regional spillover.

How Indian Americans Went From Model Minority to Political Target

▶️For decades, Indian Americans were held up as the model minority: highly educated, economically successful, entrepreneurial, and seemingly assimilated into American life. But increasingly, that success - and visibility - has begun to make them a political target.

▶️On October 11, Alexandros Paporakis, 19, was arrested after authorities received information about a potential attack targeting the Sri Venkateswara Swami Balaji Temple in Illinois. His manifesto described Indians as 'subhumans' and outlined a plan to kill as many of them as possible. His rifle got jammed, else the shooting would have very likely happened.

▶️A February 2026 protest in Frisco, Texas, where white activists warned of an alleged “takeover” by Indians, offers a revealing entry point. The episode was followed by protests outside Hindu temples, anti-Indian rhetoric over H-1B visas, attacks on Indian cultural institutions, and a surge of xenophobic commentary online.

▶️What happens when a minority once celebrated as proof of the American Dream becomes a symbol of the very forces — globalization, immigration and demographic change — that parts of America’s political right increasingly oppose?

▶️Indian immigration has a long history of exclusion, from early agricultural laborers confronting racist restrictions to the post-1965 immigration wave and the explosive growth of Indian professionals through the H-1B program.

▶️Today, Indian Americans occupy prominent positions in technology, business, academia and government, while becoming increasingly visible in electoral politics.

▶️Did the “model minority” label ever offer genuine belonging — or merely conditional acceptance?  Economic anxiety, immigration politics, demographic change and the growing political visibility of Indian Americans are reshaping that bargain.

▶️At its heart is a paradox: Can a community achieve the American Dream and still be told it does not look American enough?

Session LIII
Introduction
Serial murder is one type of homicide which involves the killing of three or more people
for one month and is characterized by a period of cooling off. The cooling-off period is a time
whereby the killers do not commit any murder (Knight, 2006, p. 1192). The people who commit
serial murder are known as serial killers. The crime is not recognized in the United States., as
there is no current legal code on it. In the history of serial killing, the earliest recorded case of
serial killers was in 69 CE in the Roman Empire. The serial killer by the name Locusta was
executed for poisoning individuals from the royal family. In the middle ages, there were serial
killers recorded in European countries (Vronsky, 2018, p. 15). It has likely been occurring in
other parts of the world, though it might not be recorded. Research has attempted to suggest
explanations of the behavior of serial killers and provide an analysis of their personal
development (Ostrosky & Alfredo, 2017, p. 70). There are two types of serial killers, such as
child and adult serial killers, in essence (Harmening, 2014, p. 102). A great number of theories
has been developed to address their actions. Most serial killers have psychological issues, and it
is through killing that they feel satisfied. History has introduced many serial killers, who are
adults, but in recent decades the cases connected with children, who are serial killers, are
becoming frequent. They are dangerous, just like the adults, as they indicate the same
psychological behavior (Knight, 2006, p. 1198).
Types of Serial Killers
Hedonistic Serial Killers
These are serial killers, who receive pleasure from killing, and thus the experience of
murder gives them pleasure. There is a strong link between the violence of the murder and the
sexual gratification. They can have sex with the victim before or after killing the victim (James
& Proulx, 2014, p. 595). They plan their crime well, and they dismember the body of the victim
after the murder. They have an insatiable hunger when they feel that it could be satisfied only by
killing. An example of a serial killer of this category is Jeffrey Dahmer, who was a serial killer in
the period between 1978 and 1991 (Ostrosky & Alfredo, 2017, p. 77).
Power and Control Serial Killers
These serial killers need to exercise their power and control the victim. They first
humiliate the victim, torture, and then kill their victim. They do not respect the law of the land,
and they feel that they are above the law. They also seek sexual gratification. Their main goal is
to gain power and domination, and thus killing makes them feel powerful and in control. Anyone
they feel to be threating to them is killed as they assert dominance (Vronsky, 2018, p. 49).
Visionary Serial Killers
The serial killers in this category are considered psychotic, as their visions and other dark
forces compel them to commit murder. Whoever these voices and visions tell them to kill; these
killers go ahead and kill them. Some of them have undertaken psychiatric tests, which proved
their being mentally unstable. Some of this type of serial killers are possessed by evil forces,
which drive them to kill.  
Mission-Oriented Serial Killers
These are considered as ordinary persons, and they kill a particular group of people. They
may focus on killing people from a specific religion, social class, or race. Their goal is to
eliminate the group or exterminate as many of its members as possible. An example of these
serial killers is Joseph Paul Franklin, who killed young black males, because they had white
girlfriends (Vronsky, 2018, p. 78).
Characteristics of Serial Killers
There are numerous characteristics of serial killers, and these are some of them. First,
serial killers indicate varying levels of psychopathy, which leads to destructive tendencies. They
are mostly categorized in the type of visionary serial killers. They see things and forces which
compel them to kill certain people or group of people. After their action, psychotic serial killers
are gratified and do not show any remorse. In normal circumstances, they are charming and
brilliant. Psychiatrists have identified that these people can be dangerous because people will not
know if they are vulnerable until they become victims of their psychopathic actions. (Ostrosky &
Alfredo, 2017, p. 73). The second characteristic is that when they were young, most serial killers
were abused in the family. The abuse might have been emotional, physical, and sexual. This
abuse causes them to be bitter and sometimes seek revenge by killing people (Knight, 2006, p.
1194).
The other characteristic of serial killers is that they are aroused by the activity, and they
find pleasure in the action. Another aspect is that some of them experience one or all the
Macdonald triad predictors of future violent behavior. The Macdonald triad predictors are a
fascination with fire-setting, involvement in sadistic actions, and bed-wetting (Seltzer, 2013, p.
112). The serial killers were isolated during their childhood and teenage years. This isolation
involved bullying, and the person is seeking to prove that no one can bully him or her since he or
she has grown up. Some of the serial killers’ targets are people who bullied them or showed
particular behavior associated with bullying (Carlisle, 2017, p. 17). Some other characteristics
are that the serial killers might have been involved in petty crimes, and they had trouble staying
employed (Ostrosky & Alfredo, 2017, p.81).

text:
Six critical priorities about HEX, ranked by importance, that have escaped the DeFi space for seven years:

PRIORITY 1: HEX is two assets at once, and the one you accumulate is deflationary.

As a coin it inflates 3.69% forever.

As a share it deflates, hard. Historically, Shares deflate 7x faster than HEX inflates. The share rate has gone 10,001.1 → 46,891.3 across 2,480 days — 25.52% compound, 10.53% over the last twelve months, and zero downward moves in the entire history

Inflationary HEX locks in deflationary shares & the inflation only goes to locked time deposits.

HEX has two charts. Market Price & USD Price of one tShare

Bottom line, ~ 4.7x more HEX is needed to lock one tShare today than when the contract launched in December 2019.

The share system renews itself, and every share that expires leaves more for whoever locks next. Nobody can lock HEX for 5,556 days. Every share is a lease to sit in a Share Pool fixed to a fifteen year cycle. When a stake ends, its shares are deleted from the total and nobody inherits them. The daily payout is then divided among fewer shares & an ever-increasing Share Price for new entry. Ending stakes also mints new HEX, raising the daily Share Pool payout, forever.

HEX is not just deflationary, it's a renewing system.

PRIORITY 2: HEX makes time the scarce input (this is a big deal that takes a while to resonate).

Time sets the price of a share, and the price only goes up. The share rate is the HEX cost of one share. The code can only raise it ( if (newShareRate > g._shareRate) ); there is no branch that lowers it. It has gone 10,001.1 → 46,891.3 in 2,480 days with zero downward moves. No one can buy a share at yesterday’s price — an earlier start date cannot be bought at any price.

Longer locks get up to 3x more shares, with the bonus maxing out at 3,641 days ( LPB_BONUS_MAX_PERCENT = 200 ). The contract rewards committed time.

Every share has a mandatory expiry and no share can be extended, so dilution is a lease that runs out.

All outstanding T-Shares must expire within 5,555 days of the last stake ever started.

In a normal dilutive system claims accumulate forever and the best case is slower dilution; here the denominator is contractually guaranteed to drain. That is why the system renews rather than merely delaying.

Bitcoin's Proof of Work pays people to burn electricity; HEX's Proof of Wait pays people to give up their money for a fixed time. HEX pays the Investor for patience instead of a Bitcoin Miner for power.

HEX + Time builds a yield-generating moat.

PRIORITY 3: Retail is paid to own, control and store its own money, in its own wallet, cold storage included. Banks profit from holding your money. The average US savings account pays 0.38%, against about 4.2% for the best accounts, a gap worth $397.3B a year (§19). Nobody holds that position in HEX: there’s no custodian, no shared pool, no owner and no fee.

PRIORITY 4: The contract has no external data dependency beyond the consensus clock. This property deserves to be stated precisely because it is genuinely unusual.

HEX requires no oracle price feed, no interest-rate input, no collateral ratio, no liquidation engine, no governance vote, no human operator and no off-chain data of any kind. It does not know the price of HEX, ETH, gold or anything else, and the share system never asks. Everything it needs is internal: how much HEX was committed, for how long, what the share rate was at entry, and what inflation and penalties entered the reward pool. It derives the current day from block timestamps and rolls over at 00:00:00 UTC. Issuance is a fixed 0.009955% of allocated (total minted) supply per day — a constant applied to a number the contract already holds.

HEX also has no owner, no admin, no pause, no proxy and no fee parameter.

Nobody can change the terms, take a spread, or stop it. This is what makes the fifteen-year term credible, and it is the one thing no bank product can offer at any price.

PRIORITY 5: The yield is a guarantee, not a promise, because there is no promisor.

There is one assignment to the payout total in the entire contract, zero setter functions, zero owner checks, no admin and no pause. And the payout is newly minted, not drawn from a reserve — so there is no pot to run dry, no borrower to default, no bank to fail, and no counterparty whose solvency you are relying on.

PRIORITY 6: Depth is a market condition here, not a property of HEX, and it has been 225x deeper. On eHEX’s all-time-high day (19 Sep 2021) the Ethereum pool held $68.76 million of liquidity, peaking at $86.25 million on 8 Feb 2022, against $306,173 by June 2026 — a 281.7x decline. But liquidity providers never left. The pool held 58.76 million HEX on the ATH day and 167.82 million HEX today — 2.86x MORE HEX — while the dollar value fell 224x. The depth collapse was a price effect, not a withdrawal of liquidity. Nobody needs permission to change it: liquidity on PulseX is globally sourced, anyone can add it, and it follows volume.

The New York Sun’s October 17 report adds to the growing international media coverage of Somaliland and its push for U.S. recognition. It highlights President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Irro)’s offer to open Berbera Port to Washington, develop opportunities around Somaliland’s mineral resources, and name an airport after President Donald Trump.

The report frames these proposals as part of a broader effort to build a strategic partnership with the United States. It also notes that Israel has recognized Somaliland, while the U.S. State Department has not announced a decision. The coverage brings renewed attention to Somaliland’s location, resources, and ambitions for stronger international ties.

Automotive & EVsNdFeB Magnets for traction motors, power steering, and cabin electronics.Assembly line halts. Automakers like Ford have had to idle entire assembly plants for weeks purely for want of magnets. This pauses downstream shipping, logistics, and dealership inventories.
Defense & AerospaceHeavy REEs (Samarium, Dysprosium) for F-35 jets, missile guidance, and radar.Production delays. High-performance defense components cannot substitute these materials. The defense industrial base faces an existential lag as munitions production timelines stall.
SemiconductorsGallium & Germanium for high-frequency microchips and optics.Foundry bottlenecks. Without high-purity gallium, next-generation power electronics and radar equipment cannot be fabricated, delaying software and hardware tech integrations.
Clean EnergyPermanent Magnets for wind turbine generators.Project stagnation. Wind infrastructure deployment slows to a crawl as the scarcity of industrial-grade turbine magnets inflates development costs.

Why the Damage is So Devastating

The leverage China holds is extraordinarily difficult to bypass in the near to medium term due to three deep structural realities:
• Zero Scalable Substitutes: For high-performance electric vehicles and advanced defense systems, there are no immediate alternative materials that offer the same magnetic density or thermal resistance. [1] (https://t.co/OlChF1DQW6)
• The "Mine-to-Magnet" Asymmetry: While the U.S. has ramped up domestic mining at facilities like the Mountain Pass Mine, extracting the rock is only half the battle. The U.S. still lacks the mature, scaled chemical refining capacity to convert those mined oxides into metals and actual finished magnets at scale, historically relying on China to finish the job. [1] (https://t.co/inftsHuBVJ), [2] (https://t.co/2Axl6HmKGy), [3] (https://t.co/iRCIfilWoc)
• Targeting the "Lifeboats": Realizing that the U.S. is trying to build domestic resiliency, Beijing explicitly blacklisted pioneering American mine-to-magnet firms like MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. By blocking Chinese shipments of critical processing inputs directly to these two companies, China aims to suffocate the exact U.S. programs meant to break its monopoly. [1] (https://t.co/xsO5juUetw), [2] (https://t.co/kd17iJ3veY)
Ultimately, the export ban reveals that in a highly globalized assembly environment, a nation does not need to block a finished product to destroy an industry; they only need to withhold a few grams of a critical material at the base of the mountain to trigger a landslide across the entire economy. [1] (https://t.co/6YJA3Mm67D), [2] (https://t.co/Hj6t9ly5G8)

text:
A great summary:
"Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸
And since honesty is so rare in my politics, let me confess a few things.

1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.

1967. After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three noes. Fifty years later, I still have no state. Turns out, rejection doesn't pay the rent.

Oslo, 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try it." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I haven't had elections in nearly 20 years. Hamas kills dissenters in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on TV teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.

Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.

Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a tech powerhouse, farms in the desert, cities from dust. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of displaying honor, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I showed only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I pretend to be surprised when Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced I don't want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I glorify death over life? Israel's fault. Responsibility isn't my strong suit.

I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hate.

And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit."

That represents a massive jump from May, when the startup was valued at $61 billion following a venture round. While co-founder Palmer Luckey continues racking up multi-billion dollar Pentagon contracts, CEO Brian Schimpf made it clear they are in no rush to IPO.

Taking the company public brings daily stock distractions, whereas staying private and buying out staff lets them laser-focus on ramping up critical military production lines. Funding your own secondary liquidity on an unprecedented scale to dodge Wall Street noise is becoming the ultimate playbook for elite deep-tech giants.

October hike odds reached roughly 44% after CPI, then faded to 17% Friday; odds of a hike by December remained 89%. Meanwhile, haven buying during the tech sell-off pushed the 10Y from 5.24% to 5.09% for the week and the 30Y from 5.60% to 5.43%.
