text:
Paraguay is a beast like no other. 🇵🇾

It pulls you in, tests your patience, drives you mad at times and somehow makes you miss it the moment you leave.

I love travelling. I always have. And I’m fortunate enough to have several places around the world that feel like a little piece of home.

When I return to Australia, I spend time with family on the farm, escape into the mountains and always find my way back to the beaches where I spent half my life. I love every minute of it. The family, the memories, the landscapes. There’s something special about visiting to the places that made you who you are.

But something strange happens after 2 or 3 weeks.

I genuinelly start missing Paraguay.

Of course, that doesn’t stop me travelling.

I’ll often head to Vietnam for a few weeks. A country I thoroughly enjoy. The energy, the people, the food, the beautiful chaos of everyday life.

Then next, Japan, to catch up with childhood friends living in Tokyo, eat incredible food and immerse myself in a culture that never seems to run out of wacky ways to fascinate me. I could spend 3 months a year in Japan & never get sick of it.

Then Dubai. A few weeks with good friends, enjoying the finer things in life & spending considerably more money than I ever want to. They should say "When in Dubai", rather than Rome.

Then one of my fav places on earth, the Greek islands.

Now, Greece is something different altogether. My family’s island, our roots, a place that will always hold a piece of my heart. Long afternoons swimming in the Mediterranean, awesome food, sunshine, music, love, dancing, wine and laughter. No rush, no particular agenda. Similiar to latin culture. Just enjoying being alive.

It's a very special 2nd home to me. 

Then always a few days in Spain, a little exploring, some good meals and a direct flight back to Paraguay.

And here’s the funny thing.

Always, after all those beautiful countries, incredible experiences, old friends & familiar places, I’m genuinely at peace to return to Asunción.

Not because Paraguay is more beautiful than Greece, more organised than Japan, more exciting than Vietnam, or wealthier than Australia.

It isn’t. And never will be.

Paraguay is rough around the edges. Sometimes it feels like the 1st world, sometimes the 2nd, and occasionally the 4th. All on the same street.

Things break. Things take forever. Simple tasks become unnecessary adventures. Some days the country tests every ounce of patience you possess.

And yet, we love it.

Because when we arrive back in Paraguay, something inside us settles.

We're back at our safe haven. Our home base. Our little corner of the world where we can switch off all the noise, forget the madness happening elsewhere & simply enjoy living.

There’s no great pressure to be anywhere. No constant feeling that we're missing anything. No feeling guilty for being alive, & no looking over your shoulder.

I wake up, enjoy spending time with my family, good friends, eating well, laughing, working on things I enjoy & taking life one day at a time.

And that’s a wonderful kind of freedom.

I’ve come to realise that loving a place and wanting to live there are two very different things.

I love Australia, Vietnam, Japan, Greece and Spain. Am impressed by Dubai. Each offers something extraordinary and each gives me new memories every time that I’ll carry for the rest of my life.

But Paraguay gives me something different.

Freedom.

And perhaps that’s the greatest luxury of all. To travel the world, experience wonderful places, and still have somewhere you genuinely look forward to return to.

The older I get, and the more of the world I see, the more I appreciate that feeling.

Paraguay isn’t perfect.

But somehow, this strange, frustrating, beautiful little country has become the place where I feel most at peace.

And the more I travel, the more I realise something I never expected.

Paraguay feels more like home than the country where I was born. 🇵🇾

Portland Fellowship is the primary local ministry in Portland, Oregon, that matches what you’re describing.
It is a long-running, interdenominational Christian ministry (founded in the late 1980s) focused on people who experience unwanted same-sex attraction (SSA) or related conflicts with their faith. Their stated approach centers on discipleship, biblical teaching, accountability, peer support, and identity in Christ rather than clinical “conversion” or orientation-change therapy. They explicitly say they are not a mental-health agency and do not practice reparative/conversion therapy.
Contact details:
•  Website: https://t.co/3H0ivxat4F
•  Phone: 503-235-6364
•  Email: office@portlandfellowship.com (or check the site for current contact options)
•  Mailing address: PO Box 14841, Portland, OR 97293
What they offer that fits your request:
•  Discipleship programs such as “Taking Back Ground” (in-person in Portland and online versions) for men and women seeking to live out their faith in the context of unwanted SSA.
•  Support groups, including for family members (“Hope Group”).
•  Peer-to-peer support and training elements; many involved have personal experience with these struggles and describe themselves as having found freedom or transformation through Christ. Staff and participants often go on to encourage or minister to others in similar situations.
•  They are connected to the national Restored Hope Network (a network of similar ministries).
Leaders and materials emphasize walking in relationship with Christ, repentance from sin (as they define it), and not being controlled by desires, with some testimonies of identity or attraction shifts (though they stress the primary goal is not “gay to straight”).
